One degradation on an images-only rollback: v0.16.2's GET /v1/admin/clients/{id}/withdrawal-payouts returns maturityId null for an early-exit payout, which its admin app rejects as malformed (strict AdminWithdrawalPayout), so that client's Maturity-tab payout list shows its read failure until roll-forward. Nothing is lost or written. No other v0.16.2 code reads withdrawal_operations.maturity_id (git grep 00e1c01). The new release filters those rows out of that list.

Erasure (convention-11): classified in clientErasureCoverage (subject FK, actor FK, request_id as codes); inspect counts it as a money record and lists it as owned; G3 deletes it before admin_sip_schedules (unreachable in practice: an early exit always has ledger and payout rows, which force G2); G2 keeps it unchanged (no contact or free-text column); a pending early-exit payout blocks erasure via the existing open-withdrawal blocker. release_manager/docs/client-erasure.md updated.

Defaults taken: refusals are schedule not active, zero value, a marked maturity or a client choice awaiting confirmation ('being settled'), a maturity date already reached ('matured': resolve the maturity instead), a ledger entry dated after today, and a changed value or schedule version. The body carries expectedValuePaise from the preview. Reopening an early-closed schedule is refused (Q-043).

Defaults taken: notification kind client_value_updated, payload {fundId, scheduleId, earlyExitId, deepLink '/activity'}; email states amount and that the payout is awaited, no bank details or references. 'Early exit' labels match the ledger entry id from the new reads, never reason_code. Receipts list only recordings, so the Receipts screen gains a separate Early exits list. Statements: a note under the table (web print view; APK page limited to its period), worded 'withdrawn' since the payout may still be pending.

Reviewer: a holding below its principal exits with principal > 0 and value 0 (withdrawal shape forbids principal portion above the amount), exactly as a maturity withdrawal does; erasure then stays refused until a correction. The preview GET reuses locking readers inside a short transaction. No frontend test added: the backend refuses a second exit whatever the key.

F1 (HIGH): accepted by the maintainer as DEC-59; no redesign, early-exit payouts stay in withdrawal_operations with maturity_id NULL. Rollback note added to DEPLOY.md, section 'Database rollback semantics', after the destructive-boundary paragraph: after 073 an images-only rollback to v0.16.2 is degraded for a client with an early exit; the v0.16.2 admin app cannot load that client's maturity payout list (payout cannot be marked paid until roll-forward); v0.16.2 lets an early-closed schedule be reopened, and after roll-forward a second early exit on it is refused with 409 STATE_CONFLICT and writes nothing. Nothing is lost. No new document.

F2 (MEDIUM): SipEarlyExitPanel renders, after done, a ClosedEarly view built from the command result (amountPaise, payout.principalPortionPaise/growthPortionPaise, effectiveDate, cancelledMaturityDate, fundName); the refetched preview is no longer shown once done. The onSettled invalidation is unchanged, so a rejected exit still refreshes the preview figures.

F3 (LOW): SipEarlyExitPanel and SipScheduleEditor report a held write (pending or unknown outcome) through onHoldChange, the EarlierInvestmentForm pattern; SipScheduleSection disables Manage and Early exit on every row while held and shows one line saying why. The editor was included (rule 15) because the new Early exit action could unmount a held editor write too.

F4 (LOW): two new refusals in earlyExitRules.ts, read under the schedule lock before any write: already_closed_early (sipScheduleRepository.wasClosedEarly, the same reader the reopen guard uses) and principal_below_zero (principal < 0 with value > 0). Both return 409 STATE_CONFLICT and show in the preview's refusal. Contract SipEarlyExitRefusalCode gained the two values (new unreleased operation only); OpenAPI regenerated; frontend operations unchanged by the generator.

F4 proof: refusal test now also covers a holding at principal -50000 / value 100000 (seeded with a maturity_reinvestment entry of -150000 principal) and a schedule exited, reopened by SQL as v0.16.2 would, given a new contribution, then exited again. Controls (each reverted, sha256 checked): 20261116T130108Z-2218850 principal_below_zero removed -> 500 at the CHECK, red; 20261116T130125Z-2226443 already_closed_early removed -> 500 at sip_early_exits_schedule_uk, red.

F6 (copy): panel now says the holding's value goes to zero, and if the value is below the amount invested the invested amount it does not cover stays on record. Email and notification copy never said 'goes to zero' and is unchanged. DEC-43's plan wording ('the holding goes to zero') is the coordinator's to note; only value goes to zero in the loss case.

F5 (LOW): left as built. The preview GET takes FOR UPDATE on the open offer and the marked maturity for one short read transaction, in the writers' lock order (no deadlock, per review-7). Dropping the locks would need non-locking twins of lockOpenForSchedule and lockOpenMaturity in the shared maturity repositories (duplicated SQL beside maturity code the lane promised not to change, plus mock changes in maturity unit tests) for a small latency gain; the command re-checks everything under lock either way.
